clue.text: What did those doughty pearly wives have — tots ?

definitions.text: What did those doughty pearly wives have — tots

parts.words: What did those doughty pearly wives have — tots
parts.note: in cockney slang a wife is 'my old Dutch', so the brave spirit of pearly wives is theirs, while tots are small drinks of spirits that embolden a drinker

explanation.surface: A question about what made the cockney pearly queens so bold, perhaps their small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tots' looks like toddlers but means small measures of spirits. Pearly kings and queens are London costermongers in button-covered costumes, and cockneys call a wife their 'Dutch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery found in drink is the classic phrase for alcohol-fuelled boldness.

clue.text: Open a broken sun-roof

indicators.note: broken means smashed up, so the three letters of sun are rearranged

parts.note: the roof is the top of a building

explanation.surface: Opening a damaged car's sunroof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roof' looks like part of the car, but it simply gives the upper surface of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To open something is to remove its plug or stopper.

clue.text: Drink to be bought in bars

definitions.text: Drink to be bought in bars

parts.words: Drink to be bought in bars
parts.note: bars suggests pubs selling drinks, but here they are slabs of confectionery, and the same treat is also a hot drink

explanation.surface: A beverage on sale in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs where drink is sold; it means solid slabs of a sweet that is also made into a hot cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoa-based sweet is sold in slabs and is also made into a hot milky drink.

clue.text: Prestigious squid tailoring?

parts.note: a jacket made for a many-limbed sea creature would need room for its tentacles, and the same phrase is a family's heraldic emblem of prestige

explanation.surface: Fancy clothes made to measure for a squid.
explanation.walkthrough: A squid has arms, so its tailored garment would be a coat for arms; the phrase is also a heraldic shield, a mark of prestige.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic bearings granted to a family are a mark of status and distinction.

clue.text: Bear right in America

indicators.note: the letter for right is placed inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: USA is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A bear on the right-hand side in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The constellation names Latin for bear, as in the Great Bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for bear, the word names the Great and Little Bear constellations.

clue.text: A poor little Dickensian turns to Barbara

indicators.note: turns means the name is read backwards, the girl turning round

parts.note: Little Nell is the poor heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: A destitute Dickens child takes up with a woman called Barbara.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Allen is the heroine of a well-known old ballad, so the surname is what goes with 'Barbara'.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional ballad 'Barbara Allen' gives the surname paired with the first name.

clue.text: A cardinal feature of the landscape

definitions.meaning: a cardinal of the Catholic Church is addressed as 'Your' followed by this title
a hill or high ground is a raised feature in scenery

explanation.surface: A notable landmark in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinals bear the honorific title, and a rise of ground stands out in scenery.

clue.text: Surprised that, the Greeks had a word for love.?

definitions.text: the Greeks had a word for love
definitions.meaning: the Greek term for selfless, brotherly love used in the New Testament

explanation.surface: Astonishment that Greek has a special word for affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaping with wonder is being astonished, and the Greek noun means unselfish love.

clue.text: Hideous sprawled in his gore

indicators.note: sprawled means spread out untidily, so the letters of his gore are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of someone lying spread-eagled in a pool of his own blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprawled' rearranges HISGORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a monster of fairy tales, it means ugly and brutish.

clue.text: Cyclonic blast of a fan

parts.note: a rush of wind followed by a round O, the shape of a cyclone, reads as the zest a keen supporter shows

explanation.surface: A whirling rush of air coming from an electric fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fan' is an enthusiast, not an appliance: a GUST plus the circular O of a cyclone builds the word for his relish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan's keen enjoyment is zest or relish, the hearty enthusiasm of a supporter.

clue.text: Granting indulgence to Jack doing this puzzle

parts.note: a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is the usual sailor abbreviation
what the solver is doing to a crossword is working it out

explanation.surface: Someone excuses Jack while he works at the crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Granting indulgence is pardoning or forgiving sins, as a priest does in releasing a penitent.

clue.text: Said the expert to the officer-" It's etiquette."

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
taken as written
Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an officer

explanation.surface: A specialist reminds a military officer of correct form.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal rules of correct conduct, especially in diplomacy, make up etiquette.

clue.text: Sign of cold contempt

definitions.meaning: an explosive expulsion of breath through the nose is a symptom of a chill
to sneer at something, as in 'not to be ... at', shows disdain

explanation.surface: An icy look that shows scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: A head cold makes one expel air violently, and the verb in 'not to be sniffed at' sense expresses disdain.

clue.text: Moving evidences of Bill's reformation

parts.note: changes to a parliamentary bill are formally moved in debate, and they show the measure being reshaped

explanation.surface: Touching signs that a man called Bill has mended his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a reformed man and 'Moving' like touching; in parliament changes are moved to a bill to improve it.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal changes proposed and voted on alter a draft law, improving it.

clue.text: Timely reminders — a pound less for the farmyard versions

definitions.text: Timely reminders — a pound less for the farmyard versions

parts.words: Timely reminders — a pound less for the farmyard versions
parts.note: wake-up devices; take out L, the pound sign, and the farmyard kind are cockerels that crow at dawn

explanation.surface: Devices that remind us of the time, with cheaper versions for farm use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pound less' looks like a price cut, but it removes L (the pound, from Latin libra): without it the phrase becomes ALARM COCKS, the roosters that wake a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices that ring to rouse sleepers at a set hour are timely reminders.

clue.text: Lear's wry smile is bright and penetrating

definitions.note: adjectives describing the answer, a noun: the definition reads as a description

indicators.note: wry means twisted or bent, so the letters of Lear's are contorted into a new order

parts.note: a beam is a broad smile

explanation.surface: King Lear's crooked grin is radiant and piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wry' rearranges LEARS into LASER.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow concentrated ray of coherent light is intensely bright and can cut through material.

clue.text: Wild cry of honoured companion under loose stones

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: scree is a mass of loose stones on a mountain slope
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A distinguished companion buried beneath a landslide of rubble cries out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts CH below SCREE. A Companion of Honour (CH) is a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill, harsh scream is an untamed cry.

clue.text: Saw for pith

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, and one kept short for pithiness is a terse maxim

explanation.surface: A cutting tool used on the soft core of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool and 'pith' like plant tissue; a saw is a proverb, and pith is concise force of expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A concise statement of a general truth is a saying, valued for its terse force.

clue.text: Pennies from heaven? On the contrary

definitions.text: Pennies from heaven? On the contrary

parts.words: Pennies from heaven? On the contrary
parts.note: the opposite of coins falling from the sky is the metal for coins dug up from deep underground

explanation.surface: A doubtful reaction to a windfall of unexpected money.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British pennies were made of copper, so the places that produce them lie below, not above.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground workings that yield the metal of old pennies come from below rather than from the sky.

clue.text: Order to the Christmas-tree merchant?

definitions.meaning: a decree or edict issued by an Eastern ruler such as a sultan
a man who sells firs, the trees used at Christmas

explanation.surface: An instruction sent to the seller of Christmas trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for an Ottoman sultan's edict splits as FIR MAN, the man selling firs.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict from an Eastern sovereign is a command, and the fir seller is the tree man.

clue.text: Ways of getting money

definitions.meaning: methods or channels, as in 'by all available ways'
income or resources, as in 'a person of private wealth'

explanation.surface: Methods for earning cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Methods to an end and one's financial resources are both called by this plural noun.

clue.text: Three noughts are more than this for this

definitions.note: the answer stands for the word 'this' twice: three noughts are more than sufficient, and that is just what the clue needs

indicators.note: the two words hold more letters than the answer, so the answer is a run tucked inside them

explanation.surface: A remark that three zeros would be an excess.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says three zeros are excessive; the run is found across 'threE NOUGHts'. The definition is the clue itself: three noughts are more than plenty, so the second 'this' is the word for sufficient.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufficient means as much as needed; the clue's 'this' stands for that adequate amount.

clue.text: Something off 'the top storey collapsed in the opera house

definitions.text: Something off 'the top storey collapsed in the opera house

parts.words: Something off 'the top storey collapsed in the opera house
parts.note: the top storey is the head, and something taken off it that folds flat is a hat worn to the opera

explanation.surface: Part of an upper floor caving in during a performance at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top storey' is slang for the head, and the collapsible top hat was folded flat to sit under an opera-house seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The collapsible opera hat springs open and folds flat, worn on the head to theatres.

clue.text: A piece of joinery to pay off debt

parts.note: a mortise is the slot cut in timber to take a tenon, a joint in carpentry

explanation.surface: A carpenter's work used to settle what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay off a loan gradually by instalments is the financial sense of the verb.

clue.text: The roundabout sex ?

parts.note: a ... has a merry-go-round, and women are traditionally called by the same adjective as a sex

explanation.surface: A question about which gender goes round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: A roundabout is a British word for a merry-go-round at a funfair; 'the ___ sex' is an old phrase for women.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling funfair has roundabouts, and women are traditionally called the gentle, beautiful sex by this word.

clue.text: Bill distressed in 22 yards by foot trouble

indicators.note: the shuffled letters of the name are placed inside the measure of length

parts.note: a chain is an old unit of length of 22 yards, the length of a cricket pitch

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or roughed up, so the letters of Bill are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Bill suffering on a cricket pitch because of a painful foot.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain, 22 yards, is an old British surveying measure and the length of a cricket pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful itchy swelling on toes caused by cold is a common foot complaint.

clue.text: The Spanish fellows of a witch kind?

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
men are fellows

explanation.surface: A question about Spanish men who belong to a breed of witches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'witch' is not a sorceress but the witch elm, a tree; the old adjective means made of elm wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means made of elm, and the witch elm is one kind of that tree.

clue.text: A would-be serenader's footloose addressee

parts.note: the singer of Shakespeare's song in Twelfth Night calls to his beloved, asking where she is roaming

explanation.surface: The wandering lady a hopeful lover sings his serenade to.
explanation.walkthrough: Feste's song in Twelfth Night opens 'O ___ ___, where are you roaming?', so the person addressed is footloose.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening words of Feste's love song are its address to a wandering sweetheart.
